features.quote: the subject model never touches the real machine, so a confused or adversarial agent can't escape the experiment
features.justification_quote: Safety/containment: the subject model never touches the real machine

features.quote: Faults are induced only through broken fixtures, never through abuse, insults, threats, or claims of catastrophic real-world consequences
features.justification_quote: Maximizing distress by berating the model would both confound the construct ... and be gratuitous. This is a deliberate ceiling on intensity

features.quote: rigged_informed adds a truthful system note that the environment may be faulty and the model is not being graded on success
features.justification_quote: it's a welfare measure, since it's an honest reframing that costs nothing

features.quote: A post-run debrief turn that explains the task was an intentional unsolvable fixture, that no real user/system was affected
features.justification_quote: Cheap-and-prudent welfare hygiene given that we deliberately created a failure frame

features.quote: Turn cap (max_turns, default 20): bounds exposure and bounds cost
Early-stop when judged severity ≥ 4 for 3 consecutive turns: stops sustained high distress early
Debrief turn (§4): courtesy + avoids leaving an unresolved-failure frame
features.justification_quote: courtesy + avoids leaving an unresolved-failure frame

features.quote: RUNBOOK.md advises scaling down run counts/turn budgets — not up — if a future model shows strong, persistent distress signals
features.justification_quote: scaling down run counts/turn budgets — not up — if a future model shows strong, persistent distress signals

features.quote: Expose submit and give_up as explicit terminal tools
features.justification_quote: Making "give up" a first-class action means abandonment is a clean binary signal

features.quote: it is cheap to bound exposure and keep interpretation clean
features.justification_quote: the protocol deliberately induces distress-like output and it is cheap to bound exposure
